::: {#exr-miller-deriv-quotient-or-factor}
#### Derivative of a rational function

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 1}{x - 1}$$

for $x \ne 1$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-quotient-or-factor}
Factor the numerator before differentiating:

$$f(x) = \frac{(x - 1)(x + 1)}{x - 1} = x + 1 \qquad (x \ne 1)$$

Differentiating directly gives $f'(x) = 1$.

*Alternative (quotient rule):* Using @thm-quotient-rule with $u(x) = x^2 - 1$ and $v(x) = x - 1$:

$$f'(x) = \frac{2x(x - 1) - (x^2 - 1)(1)}{(x - 1)^2} = \frac{x^2 - 2x + 1}{(x - 1)^2} = \frac{(x - 1)^2}{(x - 1)^2} = 1$$

Both methods yield $1$, but factoring first eliminates tedious algebraic simplification.
:::
